record.paper_title: Heavy flavors and quarkonia: highlights, open questions, and perspectives
record.original_question: Is heavy-quark hadronisation universal across collision systems, or do charm and beauty baryons and exotic heavy-flavour states reveal system-dependent hadronisation mechanisms such as coalescence, augmented high-mass baryon spectra, or non-leading-colour string formation? In particular, how will measurements of Λb0, Ξc+, Ξc0, Ωc0, Bc+, multi-charm baryons such as Ξcc+, Ξcc++, Ωcc+, and Ωccc++, and exotica such as X(3872) and Tcc+ constrain competing hadronisation models?

evidence.quote: Several models based on different developments and assumptions, like the inclusion of string formation beyond the leading-colour approximation [17], or the inclusion of hadronisation via coalescence [18], or considering a set of yet-unobserved higher-mass charm-baryon states [19], have been proposed to explain the observed experimental baryon enhancement in the different collision systems.
These heavy-flavour baryon measurements challenge the assumption of that heavy quark hadronisation is a universal process across different colliding systems.

The Λ+c is the only heavy-flavour baryon whose production was measured in nucleus–nucleus collisions and it will be of primary importance in the near future to perform experimental measurements of additional charm and beauty baryons (Λ0b, Ξ+,0c, and Ω0c) in order to further constrain model calculations based on different assumptions.

Additional possible windows to study hadronization of heavy-flavour in hadronic collisions consist in performing precise measurements of the B+c meson, which contains a b and a c quarks, multi-charm baryons, such as the Ξ+cc, Ξ++cc, Ω+cc, Ω++ccc, and exotica like the X(3872) and the T+cc.

artifact.status_search_result: Recent reviews and measurements (2024–2025) indicate that the universality of heavy-quark fragmentation fractions has been disproved by enhanced charm-baryon production in pp collisions relative to e+e−, but the underlying mechanism (coalescence, augmented higher-mass charm-baryon spectrum, or string formation beyond leading colour) remains unresolved. Measurements of Λb0, Ξc, Ωc, Bc+, multi-charm baryons, and exotica are still being pursued to discriminate among models, so the question is open.

status_evidence.title: New constraints on charm–quark hadronisation – CERN Courier
status_evidence.snippet: Conflicting results from e+e− and pp collisions raise questions about the universality of charm hadron production, particularly for charm baryons.
status_evidence.claim: Universality of charm-quark hadronisation is challenged but not resolved; further measurements are needed to discriminate models.

status_evidence.title: Studying charm hadronisation into baryons with azimuthal correlations
status_evidence.snippet: Studies are addressing the role of different hadronisation processes such as coalescence into charm hadronisation into baryons and the magnitude of their effect.
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing 2024 work continues to probe coalescence vs. fragmentation models for charm baryons, indicating the problem is still open.

status_evidence.title: Recent results on heavy flavours and quarkonia from ALICE
status_evidence.snippet: Heavy-flavour baryon production has disproved the assumed universality of the fragmentation fractions across collision systems.
status_evidence.claim: Heavy-quark hadronisation is not universal, but the responsible mechanism is still under active investigation.
